why: User priority 2026-11-08. A class-compliant USB MIDI interface (the CME 1x1, then the 2x2) on the PIO-USB host port as the MIDI Pak's in and out. It is the first device class on the host port beyond HID, so it proves the port can host other USB devices, and it meets the CoCo Zero standard's MIDI line (PIZERO-281). The Pak and its router exist already (PIZERO-287).

MIDI arriving at the Pak during playback freezes the board. MIDI in from a host-port interface goes through the same receive side, so PIZERO-305 cannot be called working until this is fixed. The post-mortem should already be on the card (soak-135).

Real CoCo MIDI software (Lyra 2.85, CoCo MIDI 3) through the Pak. PIZERO-305 is done when Lyra or another Pak program plays through the host port, so proving them first on the native port separates software problems from host-port problems.

The one live stability bug, a hang in PIO-USB's timer interrupt, about one every 3 h with the USB DAC streaming. The 11-01 DAC-off soak left no logs; a fresh one was set up on 11-05 (read from soak-119 on, 15 h or more). Waits on the card, not on code. Adding a MIDI endpoint to the same host stack (PIZERO-305) makes its rate worth watching.

Retires the biggest unknown in the directory-drive plan: what Disk BASIC's sector writes mean. A hardware trace with the existing pizero_fdctrace env, written up as the spec PIZERO-292 implements; cheap, and best done before any write code.
The first thing users see: a host directory in a drive, read by an unmodified Disk BASIC. Needs PIZERO-289; mountable by editing drives.txt on the Mac until PIZERO-293 adds it on the board.
Makes directory drives the everyday storage: SAVE, KILL and RENAME land as host files with no disk full. Needs PIZERO-290 and the write spec from PIZERO-291.

The AY chips are in (PIZERO-149) and proven with our own programs; one real piece of software playing through them is what makes the feature real for users. Lyra for the Symphony-12 is the likeliest to run today; the Sierra games wait on PSRAM.
Small, everyday experience win with nothing blocking it: whole-file writes exist, so booting back into the last game is mostly a precedence rule against autorun.
Hot-plug: every software path is disproved, but one cheap test is left (unplug and replug through the simple hub). If it works the answer is 'use a hub' and the issue closes.

Other people's screens, which the kits rest on. Since PIZERO-232 changed the HDMI audio delivery, two screens that garbled sound now play it cleanly; the dev monitor and the upstairs Samsung still need a recheck (PIZERO-233). One LCD remains odd on both picture and sound (PIZERO-120, PIZERO-234), and a Raspberry Pi at 640x480p60 on it would tell monitor from signal. Opportunistic: whenever a screen is to hand.
